headline: Rock Art Protection and Hoodoo Access Management
reservation: Access to the restricted archaeological preserve is by guided tour only, which must be booked through the Alberta Parks system. While the main hoodoo trails are open for general exploration, specific areas containing sensitive First Nations rock art are strictly off-limits to unescorted visitors.

days.title: Sacred Landscapes and Hoodoo Trails

stops.name: Hoodoo Trail
stops.detail: A 2.2km walk through the sandstone pillars that defines the park's geological character.

stops.name: Battle Scene Petroglyph
stops.detail: One of the most elaborate rock art panels accessible to the public, depicting a historic conflict.

days.driving: Minimal driving within the park; conditions vary
days.note: Temperatures in the coulees can exceed 35°C in summer; plan for heat.

days.title: Milk River Valley Exploration
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from Milk River Campground

stops.name: Police Outpost
stops.detail: Visit the site of the 19th-century North-West Mounted Police post located along the riverbanks.

stops.name: Milk River Kayak Launch
stops.detail: Observe the park from the water; the river provides a unique perspective on the sandstone cliffs.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes for local park roads; conditions vary
days.note: River levels fluctuate; check flows at the visitor centre before launching.

days.title: Archaeological Preserve Guided Walk

stops.name: Restricted Preserve
stops.detail: Participate in a guided interpretive tour to see petroglyphs and pictographs not accessible to the general public.

stops.name: Writing-on-Stone Viewpoint
stops.detail: A high-ground perspective showing the Milk River meandering through the prairie landscape.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour to transit from gateway towns; conditions vary
days.note: Guided tours are seasonal and frequently sell out; check official schedules.

intel.title: Day Use Limits
intel.text: The main day-use area near the beach and visitor centre fills quickly on summer weekends. Overflow parking is limited, so mid-week visits are recommended for guaranteed access.

intel.title: Border Proximity Issues
intel.text: Due to the proximity to the US border, mobile phones may frequently switch to roaming on American towers. Disable data roaming to avoid unexpected charges while in the coulees.

intel.title: Prairie Distances
intel.text: Milk River is the nearest town for fuel and basic services. There are no gas stations within the park or the immediate surrounding ranchlands.

intel.title: Summer Heat Precautions
intel.text: The park experiences extreme heat from July through August. The best lighting and safest temperatures for the Hoodoo Trail occur in the early morning.

intel.title: Cultural Protection
intel.text: Entering the Archaeological Preserve without a guide is a legal offense. Respect all signage protecting these Niitsitapi cultural sites.

plan.arrival: Arrive via Lethbridge (YQL), fuel up in Milk River, and proceed 40km east to the park entrance for check-in.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are suitable for the paved access roads; check for local closures if exploring secondary gravel prairie roads.
plan.goldenHour: The viewpoint overlooking the Milk River valley, where sandstone textures are emphasized by low-angle light.
